cars.generation: Original Gaydon VH V12 road coupe
cars.variant: DB9 coupe — 2004 launch ZF six-speed automatic
cars.specification_market: Original coupe launch release and final technical table, announcing Frankfurt September 9, 2003, reproduced as the 2004 DB9. Selected ZF automatic; manual/Graziano ratios, clutch and acceleration are not mixed in. Native 335 kW / 450 bhp at 6000 rpm, 570 Nm at 5000 rpm, 10.3:1 compression and steel brakes belong to this launch reference. Later manuals/brochures use other peak-speed/compression notation; those are not reconciled by mixing dates. Current retrospective 510-bhp/ceramic/adaptive figures are excluded, as are Volante, Sports Pack, 470-bhp revisions, facelift and GT.
cars.summary: The DB9 inaugurated Aston Martin’s Gaydon production era and the VH aluminium architecture that shaped the marque’s subsequent road cars. Its bonded and riveted aluminium structure, front-mid V12 and rear transaxle made the 2+2 a substantial engineering and design renewal of the traditional DB grand tourer.

cars.specification_market: Original Jaguar Cars English road brochure, printed publication 3294/B; technical leaf PDF6 and publisher/footer PDF8 visually read. Host filename says 1975, but its GM400 automatic column shows a later pre-HE revision; 1975 here is family introduction, not an authenticated brochure edition date. Selected four-speed manual is explicit in the technical leaf; GM400 automatic data are not manual data. Native 285 DIN HP at 5800 rpm and 294 lb-ft at 3500 rpm retained without conversion or relabelling as the heritage text’s bhp. No HE, AJ6, 6.0, facelift, convertible, XJR-S or race specification. No exact brochure year or 1975 Borg-Warner automatic claim.
cars.summary: The XJ-S established Jaguar’s international grand-touring direction with a distinctive flying-buttress coupe, V12 power and chassis development from the XJ saloon. The design retained the influence of Malcolm Sayer and William Lyons while combining performance, refinement and four-seat road use, making it an important transition in Jaguar’s sporting lineage.
